docs.title: Provider Storage
docs.text:
Declare S3 buckets, access grants, credential rotation, and lifecycle rules in a namespaced Storage resource. Provider Storage supports MinIO, AWS, Open Telekom Cloud (OTC), OVHcloud, and CloudFerro.

Platform operators start with Installation and Cloud IAM bootstrap. For bucket creation and consumer credentials, see Use Storage. Permissions explains sharing, and Backend differences describes access rules and limits. The API reference lists resource fields.

For repository development, see Local tests.

docs.title: ADR-001: Provision Storage on AWS, OTC, and MinIO
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Provider Storage offers one Storage API for AWS S3, OTC OBS, and MinIO. Each backend uses different bucket, identity, credential, and policy resources. A shared Composition would mix these provider-specific models.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Keep the Storage API independent of the backend. Use one Composition for each backend.

Each Composition must:

  1. create the declared buckets;
  2. create the consumer identity, credentials, and permissions;
  3. grant access only after it verifies the bucket owner and the matching grant;
  4. publish a consumer Secret named spec.principal in the Storage namespace, with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

An access request is intent only. Access becomes active only when the verified bucket owner sets a matching grant.

The backend resource mapping is:

Backend Bucket Consumer identity Authorization MinIO Bucket User named Policy resources AWS S3 Bucket IAM User and AccessKey IAM Policy and UserPolicyAttachment OTC wrapped OBS Bucket wrapped IAM UserV3 and CredentialV3 OBS BucketPolicy with user IDs

Provider-kubernetes Object resources wrap resources that cannot be composed or observed directly.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A new backend needs a new Composition and backend-specific tests.
  • S3 compatibility does not prove correct provisioning or authorization.
  • Grant logic must verify bucket ownership and discoverability.

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• Peer lookup uses the Storage discovery label. It does not enforce the per-bucket discoverable flag as a condition for a grant.
  • Provider-kubernetes has broad access to provider resources and Secrets. Platform RBAC is part of the security boundary.

docs.title: ADR-002: Rotate Static Credentials by Generation
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: For backends that issue static access keys, an immediate key replacement can break a consumer that has not reloaded its Secret. Keeping too many old keys increases the security risk.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use spec.credentialsRollover to define the active credential generations:

  • interval is daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly, or none;
  • maxToKeep is the total number of active generations, including the current generation;
  • the default is interval: none and maxToKeep: 1;
  • maxToKeep must be 1 when interval is none.

A time-based generation uses the current UTC period. The suffix format is:

Interval Suffix format daily -YYYYMMDD weekly -YYYYwWW monthly -YYYYMM quarterly -YYYYqQ yearly -YYYY none No suffix

A Composition must calculate the generation once per reconciliation. It must use that value for all identities, credentials, permissions, and Secrets.

Each desired generation creates backend-specific credentials. The first generation is current. Provider Storage writes it to the stable Secret named spec.principal. Crossplane removes generations that are not in the desired set.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Consumers keep one Secret name. They must reload it before an old generation is removed.
  • An overlap gives consumers time to reload, but it also keeps more keys valid.
  • Rotation occurs during reconciliation after the period changes. It does not occur at an exact time.
  • This decision applies only to static access keys.

docs.title: ADR-003: Run Portable Lifecycle Cleanup Jobs
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The Storage API supports Delete and Notify rules. A rule can select objects by age, activation time, and prefix. Native lifecycle features differ between backends and do not provide the same behavior.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Run lifecycle rules as Kubernetes CronJobs instead of native bucket lifecycle rules.

For each Storage with lifecycle rules, the Composition creates:

  • one ConfigMap with one rclone script for each rule;
  • one CronJob with one container for each rule.

The rules work as follows:

  • Notify lists matching objects and does not change them;
  • Delete removes matching objects;
  • minAge selects objects by relative age;
  • at starts repeated processing after that time;
  • a target selects a bucket or a prefix in that bucket.

The default schedule is 17 2 * * *. Operators can change it in the storage EnvironmentConfig.

Jobs use the current consumer Secret and the backend settings from the EnvironmentConfig. They do not receive a Kubernetes service-account token. concurrencyPolicy: Forbid prevents two scheduled Jobs from running at the same time. Jobs have a deadline and a finite retry limit. Failed Pods do not restart in place. These limits prevent a failed Job from blocking later scheduled runs.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• All backends use the same Job and script generator.
  • Cleanup depends on Kubernetes, network access, rclone, and valid consumer credentials.
  • Containers for rules in the same Job run at the same time. Rules with overlapping targets can conflict.
  • An at rule runs on every later schedule. Notify can report the same object more than once.

docs.title: Current limits
docs.text:
• The API does not reject rules with overlapping targets.
  • The execution order of rules in one Job is not deterministic.

docs.title: ADR-004: Add an OVHcloud S3 Backend
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Provider Storage needs to create S3 buckets and consumer credentials in an OVHcloud Public Cloud project. The project provides OpenStack users, S3 credentials, regional buckets, and per-user S3 policies. Crossplane needs a controller identity with permission to manage these resources.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
During bootstrap, an administrator creates a dedicated OVHcloud IAM service account for the controller. The bootstrap administrator can read the project and create the service account and its IAM policy. Scope the controller policy to the target Public Cloud project and grant the actions needed to manage project users, their S3 credentials and policies, and regional buckets. The controller does not need permission to create IAM service accounts or IAM policies. Store its credentials in the provider Secret.

Use the OVHcloud Composition to create the buckets and the OpenStack users inside that project. It creates S3 credentials and a policy for each consumer user. A separate project user owns the buckets, so a consumer credential change does not change bucket ownership. The consumer receives the same credential Secret contract as for the other backends.

Use standard regional Object Storage. Keep the project ID, storage region, and S3 endpoint in the backend configuration.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
The controller service account is distinct from the OpenStack users it creates. The service account's IAM policy controls what Crossplane can manage in the project; each user's S3 policy controls access to buckets and objects.

Removing a bucket from spec.buckets, or removing its Storage resource, requests bucket deletion. OVHcloud rejects deletion while the bucket contains data. S3 policy changes can take time to affect access, so revocation is not immediate.

docs.title: ADR-005: Add a CloudFerro S3 Backend with Project Boundaries
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
CloudFerro uses OpenStack projects for identity and Ceph for S3-compatible object storage. A Keystone EC2 credential belongs to one user and one project. CloudFerro bucket policies identify another project as arn:aws:iam::<PROJECT_ID>:root.

Users with S3 access in the same project can access that project's containers. Separate credentials can be revoked separately, but they do not isolate buckets between users in one project.

Provider-openstack reads the project scope from its JSON authentication configuration. A ProviderConfig has no separate field that overrides the project in that configuration.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use the OpenStack project as the CloudFerro team and S3 authorization boundary. Assign separate projects to teams that need isolation.

Before Storage reconciliation, an administrator creates a controller user without a default project, assigns the configured member role in each selected project, and verifies project-scoped Object Storage access. The administrator must have permission to create the controller user in the domain and assign the project role. The controller user needs only the configured project role.

Operators provide one namespaced controller Secret for each project. Its name is cloudferro-project-<project-id> and its key is config. The JSON value contains the controller credentials and the project ID as tenant_id. Operators create a namespaced OpenStack ProviderConfig that refers to this Secret. A project EnvironmentConfig holds storage.projectId, storage.providerConfigName, endpoint, and region settings. The project ID must match the Secret's authentication scope.

A Storage selects the generic Composition and its project EnvironmentConfig:

metadata:
  annotations:
    storages.pkg.internal/environment: storage-cloudferro-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
spec:
  crossplane:
    compositionSelector:
      matchLabels:
        provider: cloudferro

All OpenStack managed resources for a Storage refer to the ProviderConfig named by its EnvironmentConfig. Storages in one namespace can share the project ProviderConfig. The Composition does not create or own it. ContainerV1 uses the project from the Secret. EC2CredentialV3 uses the current auth scope; the Composition does not pass projectId or userId.

The Composition creates buckets with ContainerV1 and one EC2 credential for each retained Storage credential generation. It publishes the standard consumer Secret. It does not create OpenStack users or role assignments.

For an active cross-project grant, the Composition resolves one discoverable Storage with the matching principal. It resolves that Storage's EnvironmentConfig and creates an AWS S3 BucketPolicy with the grantee project's root ARN. It does not use a peer ProviderConfig lookup. The Composition still creates an AWS ProviderConfig from its generated EC2 credentials for S3 bucket policies. Pending requests and None grants do not add access.

The environment selector is an authorization selector. Admission controls must limit which users and namespaces can select each project environment. Only trusted operators can change project EnvironmentConfigs or ProviderConfigs. Secret read access must be limited to provider workloads and trusted operators.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Every S3 user in one project can access that project's buckets. EC2 key rotation and revocation do not provide user-level bucket isolation.
  • The runtime controller receives a project member role. It does not receive user-administration or role-administration permission.
  • One shared controller user can serve many projects. Separate controller users also work because every project Secret contains a complete identity.
  • Compromise of a shared controller password affects all projects assigned to that user. Separate per-project Secrets reduce Kubernetes access scope but do not change the OpenStack identity scope.
  • The IAM bootstrap owns OpenStack identities and role assignments. Operators apply project Secrets, OpenStack ProviderConfigs, and project EnvironmentConfigs. A platform can generate the two configuration resources from project Secret names with Kyverno. The Composition owns only its internal AWS ProviderConfig.
  • EnvironmentConfigs are cluster-scoped. Each Storage namespace needs its own OpenStack ProviderConfig and project Secret. A shared project EnvironmentConfig needs one source of configuration.
  • Operators must review dependent Storage resources before removing controller users, role assignments, or project Secrets.
  • Removing a bucket requests deletion under Crossplane's default management policy. The Composition does not force deletion of a non-empty bucket.

docs.title: ADR-006: Use One Standalone IAM Bootstrap Script
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Cloud IAM setup needs privileges that Crossplane does not need during normal operation. Operators have different requirements for credentials, network access, and automation. They need to choose where and when to run bootstrap.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Operators choose where and when to run IAM bootstrap: on a specific host, in a CI/CD pipeline, or on a local machine.

Provide one standalone script, scripts/bootstrap-iam.sh, for AWS, OTC, OVHcloud, and CloudFerro. Include its policies and helpers so operators can run it without a repository checkout.

Keep IAM bootstrap separate from Storage reconciliation and Kubernetes deployment. The script prepares cloud identities and permissions and can render controller Secrets. Operators deploy those Secrets through their chosen deployment process. The script does not need Kubernetes access.

Crossplane uses only the controller credentials or workload identity needed for runtime operations. It does not use the privileged bootstrap login.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The same script supports manual and automated operator workflows.
  • Operators control access to the bootstrap login and generated credentials.
  • Cloud IAM setup and Kubernetes deployment remain separate steps.

docs.title: Consumer credentials
docs.text: Provider Storage publishes S3 access keys in a stable consumer Secret. Provider credentials are separate: Crossplane uses them to manage cloud resources. They must never appear in a consumer Secret. See Cloud IAM bootstrap.

docs.title: Secret contract
docs.text:
The Secret uses spec.principal as its name and the Storage namespace. Every backend publishes these keys:

  • AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  • AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

Connection settings can add AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_REGION, and AWS_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE. Initial provisioning creates no consumer Secret until both required keys are available. During replacement, the Composition keeps the previous Secret and reports it as not ready until the new pair is available. It copies only the documented keys from the new source.

spec.providerIdentity can set a shorter provider-native name. It does not change the principal or consumer Secret name. Provider-native connection Secrets, such as <principal>-credentials or <principal>-<generation>, are internal. Consumers use the stable Secret.

Static S3 keys work with the supported backends and common S3 clients, including AWS SDKs and rclone. They do not depend on the cloud that hosts Kubernetes. Their holders can use them outside that cluster, so Secret read access gives access to the associated cloud permissions.

docs.title: Rollover
docs.text:
ADR-002 defines retained credential generations. Provider Storage writes the current generation to the stable Secret and removes generations outside maxToKeep.

Consumers must reload that Secret or restart before the overlap ends. Provider Storage does not force a reload. Rotation occurs on reconciliation after a period boundary; it does not provide an exact expiry time. Function response caching can delay it.

Keeping the Secret does not extend a credential generation's validity. Use more than one retained generation when consumers need an overlap.

A Ready condition does not prove S3 authorization. Verify allowed and denied operations, retained keys, and revocation with the issued keys.

docs.title: Storage and access
docs.text: Limit each identity to the declared buckets and grants where the backend allows it. Enable Kubernetes Secret encryption at rest and restrict Secret read access. Keep credentials out of Git, logs, and status fields. Use an external secret manager when the deployment requires it.

docs.title: Backend differences
docs.text: Each backend Composition maps the Storage API to its provider's bucket, identity, and access resources.

docs.title: Where access rules live
docs.text: Backend Bucket Identity and credential Access rule MinIO Bucket User with generated credentials Named Policy resources; the User lists their names. AWS S3 Bucket IAM User and AccessKey IAM Policy resources linked to the user by UserPolicyAttachment. OTC OBS Bucket IAM UserV3 and CredentialV3 One OBS BucketPolicy per bucket, with user IDs in Principal. OVHcloud Regional S3 ProjectStorage Project User and S3Credentials One consolidated S3Policy document per user, linked by its observed numeric user ID. CloudFerro Project-scoped OpenStack ContainerV1 One shared Keystone controller user with one EC2CredentialV3 per Storage generation The project owns access. An AWS S3 BucketPolicy uses the CloudFerro endpoint to share with another project's root ARN.

docs.title: Backend limits
docs.text:
Storage namespaces separate Kubernetes objects. The API does not enforce which backend, environment, principal, or CloudFerro project a tenant can select. Deployments need admission and RBAC rules for these choices.

OVHcloud uses a separate, stable project user as the bucket owner. Consumer credential users can rotate without a change to the bucket owner ID. Each credential user has one combined S3 policy.

OTC must observe grantee user IDs before it can build bucket policies. It resolves each grantee through a discoverable peer Storage and observes each of that peer's retained credential users. Policies include the observed retained owner and grantee identities and omit expired generations.

CloudFerro selects a project EnvironmentConfig with the storages.pkg.internal/environment annotation or label. Its storage.projectId and storage.providerConfigName define the project and an existing OpenStack ProviderConfig. Operators create the ProviderConfig and its project Secret before Storage reconciliation. Every user with S3 access in that project can access its containers. Separate credentials do not isolate users in one project.

For cross-project access, CloudFerro resolves the grantee Storage's EnvironmentConfig and uses storage.projectId for the grantee project's root ARN. Supporting resources keep the EC2 credential and AWS provider configuration until the bucket policy is deleted. Admission rules must restrict who can select each project.

docs.title: From request to access
docs.text:
The requester records a target bucket in bucketAccessRequests. The bucket owner records its decision in bucketAccessGrants. These are fields on Storage resources; no backend creates a separate cloud request resource. The owner's grant selects ReadOnly, WriteOnly, ReadWrite, or None. The permission guide shows the resource fields and an example.

Backend Request pending, with no owner grant Owner grants access Owner sets None or removes the grant MinIO The request adds no policy name to the requester's User. The owner creates a named grant Policy; the requester lists that policy on each retained User. The requester stops listing the policy. With None, the owner's named policy has no allow statements. AWS The request creates no UserPolicyAttachment for the target bucket. The owner creates an IAM grant Policy; the requester attaches it to each retained IAM User. The requester has no attachment. With None, the owner omits the grant policy. OTC The request field does not change the generated policy. The owner's grant adds allow statements for the observed grantee ID to the bucket's BucketPolicy, even if the grantee did not record a request. The bucket policy has no allow statements for that grantee. None does not add an explicit deny. OVHcloud Each retained requester's S3Policy gets an explicit deny for the requested bucket. The policy replaces that deny with allow statements for the granted actions. While the request remains, the policy contains an explicit deny for that bucket. CloudFerro The request has no cloud-side effect. The owner adds allow statements for the grantee project's root ARN to the bucket policy. None or grant removal adds no cross-project allow. If no active grants remain, the bucket policy is removed. This does not restrict a user who is already in the owner's project.

For the owner-label requirement and the distinction between bucket visibility and access, see Discoverable Buckets.

Removing a request also differs by backend. MinIO removes the grant policy name from the requester's users, and AWS removes the grant attachments. OTC does not use the request field, so removing it has no policy effect. OVHcloud removes the bucket-specific rule from the requester's user policy. OVHcloud then falls back to ACLs when no policy rule matches; removing a request alone does not prove that S3 access is denied. See the OVHcloud policy evaluation rules.

These descriptions are the resources the Compositions request. Cloud-side enforcement and revocation are asynchronous and need positive and negative S3 tests.

docs.title: Deletion behavior
docs.text: All bucket resources use the default Crossplane management policy. Removing a bucket from spec.buckets, or removing its Storage resource, requests bucket deletion. Deletion behavior is provider-specific. A provider can reject the request when it cannot empty the bucket or when its cloud identity lacks the required delete permission.

docs.title: Cloud IAM bootstrap
docs.text:
Use bootstrap-iam.sh to prepare the cloud identity that Crossplane uses. The script supports AWS, OTC, OVHcloud, and CloudFerro. MinIO uses its own (in cluster) controller setup.

Three identities have different purposes:

  • The bootstrap administrator creates the controller and assigns permissions.
  • The controller manages buckets and consumer identities through a ProviderConfig.
  • Consumers use the credentials that Provider Storage creates for bucket access.

Bootstrap needs broad IAM permissions to create identities and assign roles. The operator decides where and when to run it: on a specific host, in a CI/CD pipeline, or on a local machine. Protect the administrator login and generated credentials with the access controls for that environment. Deploy only the controller credential to the cluster.

Review the script and its embedded permission policies before apply. Use a bootstrap login with the permissions listed for your backend below. Crossplane does not use that administrator login.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Use Bash, jq, and GNU utilities, including stat, mktemp, and realpath. Cloud operations also need these tools:

Backend Tools AWS AWS CLI OTC OpenStack CLI OVHcloud Official ovhcloud CLI CloudFerro OpenStack CLI

Download the script and put it on your command path:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
curl --fail --silent --show-error --location \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/versioneer-tech/provider-storage/0.5.0-rc.1/scripts/bootstrap-iam.sh \
  --output "$HOME/.local/bin/bootstrap-iam.sh"
chmod 0755 "$HOME/.local/bin/bootstrap-iam.sh"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
bootstrap-iam.sh --help

docs.title: Configure and apply
docs.text:
Choose aws, otc, ovh, or cloudferro as the backend. For example:

bootstrap-iam.sh ovh configure
bootstrap-iam.sh ovh show
bootstrap-iam.sh ovh apply
bootstrap-iam.sh ovh verify

configure asks for the account or domain, project, region, and other installation settings. It saves them locally without a cloud login. Backend variables can supply prompt defaults. See the settings below for overrides.

apply needs the bootstrap administrator's cloud login. It creates or updates the controller and reuses existing credentials. verify uses the controller credential to test access; it needs no administrator login. AWS assume-role mode needs its external credential source for verification. Verify uses read-only checks and reports the target and each passed check. It checks authentication and the operations listed below. It does not prove every permission used during Storage reconciliation.

Command Result configure Saves and validates installation settings. show Shows saved settings and identity IDs without secret values. apply Creates or updates cloud resources and saves controller credentials. verify Tests controller authentication and backend access. render-secrets Prints Kubernetes Secret manifests from the local file. It makes no cloud or Kubernetes calls.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Set these variables before configure to supply prompt defaults or overrides. Use the same saved settings for later operations.

Backend Variables AWS CROSSPLANE_AWS_ACCOUNT_ID, AWS_REGION, CROSSPLANE_AWS_AUTH_MODE, CROSSPLANE_AWS_TRUST_PRINCIPAL_ARN, CROSSPLANE_AWS_RESOURCE_PREFIX OTC CROSSPLANE_OTC_DOMAIN_ID, CROSSPLANE_OTC_PROJECT_ID, CROSSPLANE_OTC_REGION, CROSSPLANE_OTC_OBS_ENDPOINT, CROSSPLANE_OTC_RESOURCE_PREFIX OVHcloud CROSSPLANE_OVH_PROJECT_ID, CROSSPLANE_OVH_API_REGION, CROSSPLANE_OVH_STORAGE_REGION CloudFerro CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_DOMAIN_ID, CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_AUTH_URL, CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_REGION, CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_ADMIN_CLOUD, CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_PROJECT_PATTERN, CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_PROJECT_ROLE

AWS IAM overrides also use the CROSSPLANE_AWS_ prefix: ROLE_NAME, ROLE_PATH, POLICY_NAME, USER_NAME, USER_PATH, USER_POLICY_NAME, MANAGED_USER_PATH, and MANAGED_POLICY_PATH. OTC supports CROSSPLANE_OTC_USER_NAME, CROSSPLANE_OTC_GROUP_NAME, and CROSSPLANE_OTC_AUTH_URL. CloudFerro supports CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_CONTROLLER_NAME.

docs.title: Local files
docs.text:
Each backend uses ~/.config/provider-storage/<backend>-creds.json. Set PROVIDER_STORAGE_CONFIG_DIR to another absolute directory, or set CROSSPLANE_<BACKEND>_CREDENTIALS_FILE for one installation. Keep these files outside Git repositories. They must be owned by you and have mode 0600; new directories use mode 0700.

The JSON has a config section for installation settings and an identity section for controller credentials. CloudFerro also saves a projects list. Administrator passwords and tokens are not saved. Later cloud commands reuse saved settings and reject conflicting variables before cloud access. Namespace and credential-file overrides are not saved. Identity metadata is not sent to providers. Secret rendering selects only the fields used by that provider.

Run configure before the first apply. Once an identity exists, use a separate file to change its account, project, or region. A CloudFerro pattern change clears the saved project selection. Run apply to select matching projects again. Earlier role grants and deployed Secrets remain; remove them separately when access must be revoked.

AWS assume-role mode saves configuration without a static credential. Use the external workload identity and assumeRoleChain in its ProviderConfig. This mode does not need a rendered controller Secret.

docs.title: Deploy controller Secrets
docs.text:
Each Composition uses a ProviderConfig for cloud authentication. For static credentials, that config points to a controller Secret. IAM apply creates the cloud identity and saves credentials locally. Secret deployment is a separate step; the IAM script has no Kubernetes client or context.

Set the namespace used by the ProviderConfig's Secret reference, then pipe the manifest to kubectl:

set -o pipefail
export CROSSPLANE_OVH_NAMESPACE=workspace
bootstrap-iam.sh ovh render-secrets |
  kubectl --context storage-cluster apply --server-side -f -

Replace storage-cluster with your deployment context. Rendering prints credentials, so keep its output out of logs. Apply the Secret in every namespace that needs it. The default namespace is workspace. pipefail makes a render failure fail the pipeline too.

Use the matching backend and CROSSPLANE_<BACKEND>_NAMESPACE variable:

Backend Controller Secret Secret key AWS static-user aws-provider-creds credentials OTC otc-provider-creds credentials OVHcloud ovh-provider-creds credentials CloudFerro cloudferro-project-<project-id> for each selected project config

Set credentials.secretRef.name, namespace, and key in the ProviderConfig to these values. For CloudFerro, create the project Secret and OpenStack ProviderConfig in each Storage namespace. The project EnvironmentConfig selects that ProviderConfig with storage.providerConfigName and records its project as storage.projectId. See the CloudFerro dependency guide for project setup.

AWS assume-role mode uses an external workload identity and role trust instead of a static controller Secret. Both AWS modes need the runtime role in assumeRoleChain. Keep project, region, endpoint, and role settings in the dependency manifests consistent with bootstrap. Follow the installation guide for provider deployment.

docs.title: Rotate controller credentials
docs.text:
AWS static-user, OTC, and CloudFerro support rotation. Prepare the replacement and check the verification result before you render or deploy Secrets:

bootstrap-iam.sh otc apply --rotate-credentials
bootstrap-iam.sh otc verify

After verification succeeds, render and apply the Secret in each required namespace:

set -o pipefail
export CROSSPLANE_OTC_NAMESPACE=workspace
bootstrap-iam.sh otc render-secrets |
  kubectl --context storage-cluster apply --server-side -f -

Rotation saves the replacement locally and verifies cloud access. AWS and OTC then delete the previous key. CloudFerro invalidates the old password when it changes the password. Existing cluster Secrets still contain the old credentials until you replace them. Allow for that interruption, then check that providers use the replacement. The IAM script does not check or update the cluster.

If rotation fails, keep the local file and rerun apply to resume it. The temporary rotation section supports recovery and blocks configuration changes and Secret rendering until rotation succeeds. If Secret publication fails, repeat the pipe with the saved credentials.

OVHcloud service-account rotation is manual. Rotate AWS workload credentials through their external identity system.

docs.title: AWS
docs.text:
Choose a controller authentication mode during configure:

Mode Source assume-role (default) Existing same-account IAM role or user, such as a workload identity. Set its trusted principal ARN. static-user Dedicated IAM user and one access key saved in the local file.

Both sources assume the controller runtime role. The bootstrap login must manage that role, its trust and inline policies, and tags. Static mode also needs permission to manage the dedicated user and access key.

The embedded runtime policy permits bucket operations under the configured prefix and identity operations under the managed IAM paths. It includes wider read and list actions needed by the provider and denies changes to the controller credential user. Managed users and policies default to /provider-storage/managed/; the controller user is outside that path.

Choose the bucket prefix before apply. Its default is aws-<account-id>. Use the same prefix for Storage resources; IAM enforces it.

verify authenticates the credential source, assumes the configured role, checks the resulting account and role, and lists S3 buckets. Set that role in assumeRoleChain for both modes. See the AWS dependency guide.

docs.title: OTC
docs.text:
Configure the domain ID, regional project ID, region, and OBS endpoint. Use an OpenStack administrator login with Security Administrator in the target domain. The script verifies domain scope before IAM operations.

Apply creates one programmatic controller user, one group, and a permanent AK/SK. The group receives Security Administrator at domain scope and OBS Administrator for all existing and future projects. The regional project ID selects the provider project, not the OBS permission scope.

Use a dedicated domain. OTC cannot restrict these system permissions to a bucket prefix, and an agency cannot receive Security Administrator. The default bucket prefix, otc-<domain-id>, is a naming rule only. IAM changes can take 10 to 15 minutes to take effect.

verify signs an OBS bucket-list request with the saved controller AK/SK. It needs curl 7.87 or later to sign the payload header. Earlier curl versions can return HTTP 400 even with valid credentials. No OpenStack administrator session is needed. The ProviderConfig reads otc-provider-creds. See the OTC dependency guide.

docs.title: OVHcloud
docs.text:
Install the official CLI and run ovhcloud login outside this repository.

The bootstrap login must read the target project, create an OAuth2 service account, and create or update its IAM policy. Apply limits that policy to the exact project. It permits the Object Storage users, roles, policies, S3 credentials, and regional storage operations used by the Composition.

The controller file is separate from the CLI login. Never use ~/.ovh.conf as its path. verify uses the saved service account to read the project and list its users. The ProviderConfig reads ovh-provider-creds. See the OVHcloud dependency guide.

docs.title: CloudFerro
docs.text:
Create and activate billing projects in the CREODIAS portal first. Bootstrap does not create projects or change wallets and billing. Assign separate projects to teams that need isolated bucket access.

Configure the domain, Keystone v3 URL, OpenStack region, bootstrap profile, and project-name pattern. Use current as the profile for an active v3token login. Patterns must start with ^ and end with $; the default is ^.+-[0-9]{4}$. Limit the pattern to projects the controller must manage.

The bootstrap login must list projects, create a user in the target domain, and grant the configured project role. The script verifies domain scope before these operations. Re-scoping a token does not add permissions.

Apply creates or reuses one shared controller user. It assigns the project role, member by default, in each matching enabled project in the domain. The controller needs no user- or role-administration permission. It manages containers and its own EC2/S3 credentials within each project.

After another project is active, rerun apply to include it:

bootstrap-iam.sh cloudferro apply
export CROSSPLANE_CLOUDFERRO_NAMESPACE=workspace
bootstrap-iam.sh cloudferro render-secrets |
  kubectl --context storage-cluster apply --server-side -f -

This reuses the controller and password. It adds grants and saves the selected project IDs; it does not revoke earlier grants. There is no separate project registration command.

Each cloudferro-project-<project-id> Secret contains the controller identity with one project scope. Create its OpenStack ProviderConfig and project EnvironmentConfig before the Storage. Restrict who can select the environment and read its controller Secret. A user with S3 access in a project can access its containers; a bucket policy cannot isolate users within that project.

verify reads each saved project's name, domain, and enabled state with the controller login. It rejects a project outside the configured name pattern before testing container listing. Each project report shows its name and ID. The integration suite also checks EC2 credential creation and S3 access. See the CloudFerro dependency guide.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Install the dependencies and configuration package for your storage backend.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
Choose a target namespace before deployment.

  • Apply Storage resources to the target namespace.
  • Apply namespaced ProviderConfig resources in each Storage namespace.
  • Create controller Secrets in the namespace named by the ProviderConfig's Secret reference. MinIO uses a separate minio namespace by default.
  • Provider Storage creates the consumer Secret in the same namespace as its Storage resource. The Secret name is the principal name.

EnvironmentConfig and Composition resources are cluster-scoped.

For the examples in these guides, create workspace:

kubectl create namespace workspace

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
You need:

  • a Kubernetes cluster;
  • kubectl access to the cluster;
  • Crossplane v2 installed in the cluster.

For example:

helm repo add crossplane-stable https://charts.crossplane.io/stable
helm repo update
helm install crossplane crossplane-stable/crossplane \
  --namespace crossplane \
  --create-namespace \
  --set provider.defaultActivations={}

Each backend's ManagedResourceActivationPolicy lists the managed resource types it uses. Selective activation requires a provider with safe-start support; older providers activate all their types.

docs.title: 1. Install backend dependencies
docs.text:
For a cloud backend, install bootstrap-iam.sh and run configure, apply, and verify as described in Cloud IAM bootstrap. Choose where to run bootstrap: a specific host, a CI/CD pipeline, or a local machine. Compositions use a ProviderConfig to authenticate cloud API calls. For static credentials, its credentials.secretRef must point to a controller Secret. IAM apply creates the cloud identity and saves credentials locally. Run verify and check its result before you render and deploy the Secret. Then configure the ProviderConfig reference:

export CROSSPLANE_OVH_NAMESPACE=workspace
bootstrap-iam.sh ovh render-secrets |
  kubectl --context storage-cluster apply --server-side -f -

Replace ovh, its namespace variable, and storage-cluster for your backend and deployment. The Secret name, namespace, and key must match the ProviderConfig. See Deploy controller Secrets for all four backends. AWS workload identity uses external trust instead of a static controller Secret. CloudFerro needs a project ProviderConfig and EnvironmentConfig before Storage reconciliation.

Follow the dependency guide for your backend to edit the manifests:

Backend Dependency guide MinIO MinIO dependencies AWS AWS dependencies OTC OTC dependencies OVHcloud OVHcloud dependencies CloudFerro CloudFerro dependencies

The dependency manifests use the same order for every backend:

Manifest Scope Purpose 00-mrap.yaml Cluster Activates the managed resource types used by the backend. 01-deploymentRuntimeConfigs.yaml Cluster Configures provider and function deployments. 02-providers.yaml Cluster Installs the providers. 03-providerConfigs.yaml Cluster or namespace Configures provider authentication. Apply namespaced configs in every Storage namespace. 04-environmentConfigs.yaml Cluster Defines endpoint, region, and backend settings. functions.yaml Cluster Installs the Composition functions. rbac.yaml Cluster Grants provider-kubernetes access and Crossplane access to native Secrets.

Edit all placeholders before you apply a manifest. Apply the numbered files in order, then apply functions.yaml and rbac.yaml.

Keep the ProviderConfig's cloud account or project consistent with the EnvironmentConfig. The default environment name matches the backend package name, such as storage-aws or storage-minio. An environment annotation is needed only to override that name. CloudFerro's supplied project manifests need this override to select a project. Manage shared functions and provider-kubernetes once. See Select a backend for environment and provider selection.

Consumer Secrets are native composed resources. A namespaced Storage can compose these Secrets even when its cloud provider has only cluster-scoped resources. Those cloud resources still need Object adapters. Crossplane cannot compose a cluster-scoped resource directly from a namespaced Storage. See Crossplane resource scope.

The provider-kubernetes runtime redacts Secret data from Object status. Keep the MinIO runtime's logging configuration to prevent credentials from appearing in provider logs.

For cleanup scheduling and Job limits, see Lifecycle rules.

docs.title: Replace a Storage
docs.text:
A new Storage can adopt existing composed resources after the old Storage releases them. Before replacing a Storage, prevent its source manifests from creating it again. Delete the old Storage with Kubernetes orphan propagation (--cascade=orphan) to keep its composed resources. Wait until the old Storage is gone and its controller references are removed.

Create the replacement in the same namespace. Keep the backend, provider configuration, project, region, principal, provider identity, and bucket names the same. The Composition can then adopt resources with the same kind and name. Preserve their external-name annotations and provider ownership markers. Consumer Secrets and credentials can be recreated if needed.

Do not use a failed deletion of a non-empty bucket as a handover method. Its managed resource can remain in deletion, which prevents reuse. The pinned MinIO provider also rejects an existing bucket when a new Bucket resource lacks its ownership marker. Keep the existing Bucket resource and its Object adapter. Recreating managed resources from cloud resources requires provider-specific import.

docs.title: 2. Install the configuration package
docs.text:
Install one Configuration package for each backend you need. Each package contains its backend Composition and depends on ghcr.io/versioneer-tech/provider-storage/api from the same release. Crossplane installs that API package once. It owns the shared Storage XRD. Only the selected backend Compositions are installed. Provider controllers, functions, and credentials are installed separately in step 1. Use the same release for all installed backend packages.

Keep dependency resolution enabled on the Configuration resources; this is the default. Do not set spec.skipDependencyResolution: true.

For later upgrades of this package layout, update the existing API Configuration to the target release, then update all backend Configurations. Crossplane does not upgrade installed dependencies automatically by default.

Older backend packages own the XRD directly. Moving that ownership to the API package needs a separate migration before upgrade. Do not delete the XRD or its CRD: this can delete existing Storage resources. The ownership migration is not provided here.

After the backend dependencies are ready, create a Configuration manifest. Use the name and package for your backend:

Backend Name Package MinIO storage-minio ghcr.io/versioneer-tech/provider-storage/minio:0.5.0-rc.1 AWS storage-aws ghcr.io/versioneer-tech/provider-storage/aws:0.5.0-rc.1 OTC storage-otc ghcr.io/versioneer-tech/provider-storage/otc:0.5.0-rc.1 OVHcloud storage-ovh ghcr.io/versioneer-tech/provider-storage/ovh:0.5.0-rc.1 CloudFerro storage-cloudferro ghcr.io/versioneer-tech/provider-storage/cloudferro:0.5.0-rc.1

Use the selected values in this manifest:

apiVersion: pkg.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Configuration
metadata:
  name: <configuration-name>
spec:
  package: <package>

Replace the placeholders with values from the table and your package version. Save the manifest as configuration.yaml, then apply it:

kubectl apply -f configuration.yaml

Check that the configuration, providers, and functions are healthy:

kubectl get configurations,providers,functions

If the cluster has more than one Provider Storage Composition, each Storage resource must select its backend explicitly. A selector is not needed when only one compatible Composition is installed. See Select a backend.

docs.title: 3. Verify the installation
docs.text:
Use the bucket example in the target namespace. Set its selector to your installed backend. Check that the Storage becomes ready and that its consumer credentials permit the expected S3 operations. See Use Storage for backend selection, credential rollover, lifecycle rules, and verification commands.

For cloud backends, keep the project, endpoint, and region in the EnvironmentConfig consistent with the settings saved by bootstrap-iam.sh.

docs.title: Local tests
docs.text:
Use the test guide to select checks and install local test tools. The unit suite uses Docker and needs no Kubernetes cluster.

From the repository root, run all backends:

docker ps
tests/unit.bash

docs.title: Integration tests
docs.text:
Tests use the dedicated provider-storage-it cluster and the explicit kind-provider-storage-it context. Use a separate KUBECONFIG file to keep this setup apart from other clusters.

Get the operator's approval before creating the test cluster:

tests/integration/create-cluster.bash
tests/integration/run.bash minio

The runner installs Crossplane, MinIO, and the providers. It creates two Storages and checks consumer Secrets, object access, and lifecycle cleanup. Other backends need cloud IAM bootstrap and provider Secrets first. The integration guide lists backend settings and the access checks.

The cluster is for a validation cycle. Remove it when the operator directs you to do so:

kind delete cluster --name provider-storage-it

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The bucket owner sets access in spec.bucketAccessGrants. Each grant names a bucket, a grantee principal, a permission, and a grantedAt timestamp.

Permission Allowed S3 operations ReadWrite List, read, write, and delete objects. ReadOnly List and read objects. WriteOnly List, write, and delete objects. None No access granted by this resource.

None can remove an allow or create a deny, depending on the backend. See Backend differences. Other cloud permissions can still provide access.

docs.title: Discoverable buckets
docs.text:
spec.buckets[].discoverable lets clients show a bucket to potential requesters. It does not grant access or restrict grants. Peer lookup uses this label on the Storage resource:

metadata:
  labels:
    storages.pkg.internal/discoverable: "true"

AWS and MinIO look up the owner and check bucket ownership and its grant. OTC and CloudFerro look up grantees to resolve their identities. Label both Storages when sharing access. OTC builds policies from the owner's grants and observed grantee IDs; a request does not change that policy.

docs.title: Request and grant access
docs.text:
This MinIO example gives analyst read-only access to reports. Both Storages are in the same namespace. Set the timestamps when you record the request and grant:

apiVersion: pkg.internal/v1beta1
kind: Storage
metadata:
  name: reports-owner
  namespace: workspace
  labels:
    storages.pkg.internal/discoverable: "true"
spec:
  crossplane:
    compositionSelector:
      matchLabels:
        provider: minio
  principal: reporter
  buckets:
    - bucketName: reports
      discoverable: true
  bucketAccessGrants:
    - bucketName: reports
      grantee: analyst
      permission: ReadOnly
      grantedAt: "2026-01-01T12:05:00Z"
---
apiVersion: pkg.internal/v1beta1
kind: Storage
metadata:
  name: reports-reader
  namespace: workspace
  labels:
    storages.pkg.internal/discoverable: "true"
spec:
  crossplane:
    compositionSelector:
      matchLabels:
        provider: minio
  principal: analyst
  buckets: []
  bucketAccessRequests:
    - bucketName: reports
      reason: Read reports for analysis
      requestedAt: "2026-01-01T12:00:00Z"

Apply both resources after installation. The consumer Secrets are reporter and analyst in workspace. To withdraw access, set the owner's grant to None or remove it. Cloud policy changes take time to affect access.

A request has no permission field. Its reason can describe the desired access, but the owner chooses the permission. Requests and grants remain on the Storage resources for operators to inspect.

See the examples for complete manifests. Verify both allowed and denied operations with consumer credentials; a successful render does not prove cloud enforcement.

docs.title: Use Storage
docs.text: Create a namespaced Storage after installation. spec.principal identifies its consumer and names the consumer Secret. spec.buckets lists owned buckets. Use buckets: [] for access requests without owned buckets.

docs.title: Select a backend
docs.text:
Set a selector to choose the backend explicitly:

spec:
  crossplane:
    compositionSelector:
      matchLabels:
        provider: minio

Provider values are aws, cloudferro, minio, otc, and ovh. The selector is required when several compatible Compositions are installed. Install packages for the backends you need. They share one Storage API package, which owns the XRD.

Each backend uses storage-<backend> as its default EnvironmentConfig name, such as storage-aws or storage-minio. These names match the backend package names. Set the storages.pkg.internal/environment annotation or label to select another environment. If you keep an existing environment named storage, select it explicitly.

The EnvironmentConfig can set storage.providerConfigName to select an existing backend ProviderConfig. When unset or blank, AWS, MinIO, OTC, and OVHcloud use provider-aws, provider-minio, provider-otc, and provider-ovh.

CloudFerro requires an explicit provider: cloudferro selector. Its supplied project manifests use separate environment names. Select one with storages.pkg.internal/environment: storage-cloudferro-<project-id>. The EnvironmentConfig defines the project ID and an existing OpenStack ProviderConfig name. See the CloudFerro dependency guide.

docs.title: Credentials
docs.text:
The consumer Secret is in the Storage namespace. It contains AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, plus configured connection settings: AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_REGION, and AWS_S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE. Use this stable Secret instead of provider-native generation Secrets.

Set spec.providerIdentity when the provider needs a shorter user name. This does not change the consumer Secret name.

Credentials do not rotate by default. Set credentialsRollover.interval and maxToKeep to retain overlapping generations. Consumers must reload the stable Secret before the previous generation is removed. Rotation occurs on reconciliation after a period boundary. See the API reference.

For Secret publication and consumer reload requirements, see Consumer credentials.

docs.title: Lifecycle rules
docs.text:
Set rules under spec.buckets[].lifecycleRules. A target can be * for the whole bucket or a prefix such as tmp/*. Delete removes matching objects; Notify lists them in the job logs.

Set exactly one time condition: minAge, such as 30s, 15m, 2h, 1d, or 2w, or at, an RFC3339 UTC timestamp. After at, each job processes all objects under the target, regardless of age. The backend EnvironmentConfig's storage.lifecycle.schedule controls when the CronJob runs.

Jobs stop after one hour and allow two retries by default. Set storage.lifecycle.activeDeadlineSeconds (1 through 86400) and storage.lifecycle.backoffLimit (0 through 10) in that EnvironmentConfig when cleanup needs different limits. Check failed Jobs before the next run.

docs.title: Access requests and grants
docs.text: The requester lists a bucket in bucketAccessRequests. The owner sets its permission in bucketAccessGrants. A request has no permission field. See Permissions for discovery and backend limits.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The shared examples cover these cases:

Manifest Behavior Joe One bucket, static credentials, and a ReadWrite grant to Jeff. Jeff Two buckets, a ReadOnly grant to Joe, weekly rotation, and lifecycle rules. Jane Access requests without owned buckets; five retained quarterly credential generations. John Daily rotation and a grant that differs from the access described in Jane's request.

Use the matching backend overlay in examples/overlays/. Set a different namespace in each overlay when you deploy several backend example suites; they use the same Storage and principal names. The CloudFerro overlay needs your project EnvironmentConfig names and omits cross-project grants.

docs.title: Verify provisioning
docs.text:
Check the Storage conditions and events in your namespace:

kubectl get storages -n workspace
kubectl describe storage s-joe -n workspace

Synced=True means reconciliation succeeded. Ready=True means the composed resources report ready. Check that the consumer Secret has both required credential keys:

kubectl describe secret s-joe -n workspace

Pass the consumer Secret to the S3 client through its credential settings. Use the endpoint and region from the Secret. Verify allowed and denied S3 operations; resource readiness alone does not prove access.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: xrd.yaml CompositeResourceDefinition defines the Storage API.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
apiVersion: pkg.internal/v1beta1
kind: Storage

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
• spec.principal: required logical user or service principal. Provider Storage also uses it as the consumer Secret name.
  • spec.providerIdentity: optional short provider-native user name. It does not change the principal or consumer Secret name.

docs.title: Buckets
docs.text:
Each bucket entry is keyed by bucketName.

spec.buckets is required but can be an empty list for a resource that only requests access.

  • bucketName: bucket name to create.
  • discoverable: optional boolean that advertises the bucket for access requests.
  • lifecycleRules: optional object cleanup or notification rules.

docs.title: Lifecycle rules
docs.text:
Lifecycle rules are configured under spec.buckets[].lifecycleRules[].

  • target: * for the whole bucket, or a prefix such as tmp/*.
  • mode: Delete or Notify.
  • minAge: relative object age such as 30s, 15m, 2h, 1d, or 2w.
  • at: RFC3339 UTC timestamp after which each job processes all matching objects.

Each rule must set exactly one of minAge or at.

docs.title: Access requests
docs.text:
spec.bucketAccessRequests[] declares outbound requests for buckets owned by other principals.

  • bucketName: requested bucket.
  • reason: optional free-text justification.
  • requestedAt: required RFC3339 timestamp supplied by the requester.

Requests do not carry a permission field. The effective permission is recorded only on the owner's matching bucketAccessGrants[] entry.

docs.title: Access grants
docs.text:
spec.bucketAccessGrants[] declares permissions granted by this principal.

  • bucketName: bucket being shared.
  • grantee: principal receiving access.
  • permission: ReadWrite, ReadOnly, WriteOnly, or None.
  • grantedAt: required RFC3339 timestamp supplied by the owner.

docs.title: Credential rollover
docs.text:
spec.credentialsRollover controls automatic credential rotation.

  • interval: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly, or none (default).
  • maxToKeep: number of active credential generations to keep, from 1 through 10. It must be 1 when interval is none.
